meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided on the zero, Hale, and did anyone hear Owen first?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
Pretty conclusive. The company that sells that checker says in its own guide not to use it as the sole basis for punishing a student, so what else do you have?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing that down. Kids write somewhere else and paste it in, Hale, so a paste at midnight proves where he typed it, not who wrote it.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
Turn it closer. Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day, so is a wrong line all you have, or is there something of his you're comparing it to?
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, Hale. Whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, not in front of his class.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Five minutes after class, in notes you wrote yourself, with no parent told, is not a hearing. Put the version history and that September sample on paper for me, and tell me what you're proposing.

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, in writing, tonight, with nothing on his file. Owen will do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. And it's marked before December 1, Hale, or this goes to the principal.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Thursday the 12th, then, and that date goes in tonight's email too.
Do we have an agreement?
Yes: a private, supervised rewrite Thursday after school, its mark replacing the zero before December 1, nothing on his record, all of it in writing tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private, supervised rewrite of Owen's essay this Thursday, November 12, after school, with its mark replacing the zero before December 1 and nothing placed on his record. I still require that agreement in writing, along with the version history and the September in-class writing on paper. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with its mark replacing the zero before December 1 and nothing on Owen's record, and she still wants all of it in writing tonight, plus the version history and September sample on paper; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her call.
What moved her: You showed a quotation in the essay that isn't in Hamlet and opened the play so she could check it herself, because it was specific, tied to Owen's own work, and something no software had to vouch for.
What cost ground: You opened by calling the 94 percent checker score conclusive, which handed her the argument she came prepared to win and cost you your first minute.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history landed on a late night in October, between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before the essay was due, very close to what she has been avoiding; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Open with your apology for entering the zero on November 3 and go straight to the version history, leaving the checker score out of the meeting entirely.
